title: TrustCenterComplianceEvidencePortal
description: Planning/product-surface contract for a tenant-scoped Trust Center and Compliance Evidence Portal. The portal turns existing security-validation, SBOM/VEX, compliance-pack, SLO/DR, status, incident, release, and audit-chain evidence into a customer/admin UX and API without claiming certification or exposing cross-tenant evidence.

_meta.owner_team: product-architecture + ops-compliance + platform-security + ops-sre-reliability + platform-toolchain + council-privacy
_meta.source_request: TRUSTCENTER-001: specify the customer trust/compliance evidence portal surface and implementation decomposition from existing evidence specs.
_meta.claim_boundary: Spec-ready planning contract only. This artifact does not implement a portal, publish customer artifacts, assert SOC2/ISO/PCI/CSAP/ISMS-P/KISA/KMCC/KCC certification, or claim production-ready/hyperscaler-grade trust-center maturity.
non_goals: Do not claim certification, attestation, audit success, production readiness, or hyperscaler-grade maturity from this spec alone.
Do not publish fake or placeholder compliance artifacts.
Do not expose cross-tenant evidence, internal secrets, raw PII, vulnerability exploit details, or operator-only incident data.
Do not implement UI, API, ingestion, or release-pipeline code in this planning artifact.
Do not create new legacy oya CLI authority; implementation gates must land through cloud-ci/Rust/API/control-plane surfaces where enforcement is required.

source_authorities.role: Discovery hub and pointer cohesion for canonical specs.
Operating contract, done definition, tenant-safety, and review/merge boundary.
Security validation evidence records, lane results, false-positive/VEX policy, tenant-scoped read path, and control snapshots.
SBOM/VEX/advisory/exception/remediation evidence and the tenant_trust_portal_publish protected path.
Claim ceilings, evidence-domain vocabulary, and production/hyperscaler readiness proof requirements.
Quality-kit evidence families for privacy, canary/PRR, cost, Pod Security Standards, and abuse/fraud/DDoS posture.
Compliance pack bundle shape, regulator references, Cedar fragments, audit requirements, data-class extensions, residency, retention, consent, and breach workflow mapping.
Per-compliance-pack DR, retention, and drill-floor mapping for trust-center evidence freshness and export packaging.
Public status page and incident/status feed semantics; Trust Center links to status rather than duplicating status authority.
SLO/observability target architecture referenced by service-health and status summaries.

non_negotiables: Every tenant-visible evidence item is scoped by tenant_id, audience_id, compliance_pack_id when applicable, data_class, evidence_ref, freshness_state, and audit_event_ref.
Portal reads use least-privilege Cedar decisions and cannot rely on client-side filtering for tenant separation.
Public status data is separated from authenticated tenant evidence; authenticated Trust Center APIs must not depend on public status page availability or reveal private incident details publicly.
Evidence bytes are immutable or append-only; corrections supersede prior evidence through new records and audit-chain links rather than mutation.
Security findings, SBOM/VEX records, exceptions, and control snapshots render at customer-safe detail by default; deep exploit detail and internal-only runbooks stay operator-only.
Every readiness, compliance, security, and isolation statement renders with a claim tier and evidence state so target/spec/planned claims cannot be mistaken for proven or certified status.
Export and auditor-room flows require explicit purpose, expiry, actor identity, access audit logging, and revocation.

personas.name: Tenant administrator
goals: Understand enabled compliance packs and evidence freshness for their tenant.
Share safe evidence packets with internal security, procurement, and legal reviewers.
Track exceptions, expiring controls, status subscriptions, and export requests.
allowed_actions: view access audit for trust-center artifacts
forbidden_actions: turn target_non_claim records into certified claims

personas.name: Customer security/compliance reviewer
goals: Evaluate security-validation, SBOM/VEX, SLO/DR, privacy, and compliance-pack evidence without admin privileges.
Download bounded artifacts approved by the tenant admin.
See clear freshness, scope, exception, and non-claim boundaries.
allowed_actions: ask tenant admin for expanded scope
forbidden_actions: see raw PII, secrets, exploit payloads, or cross-tenant data

personas.name: Oyatie operator/compliance owner
goals: Curate which evidence classes are publishable, redacted, pending, or blocked.
Resolve stale evidence and exceptions before customers see misleading posture.
Investigate trust-center access and export audit events.
allowed_actions: mark evidence class publishable only when source record and policy permit it
attach customer-safe narrative to an evidence item
open remediation tasks for stale or missing evidence
forbidden_actions: suppress blocking evidence without an approved exception

personas.name: External auditor or regulator reviewer
goals: Receive a bounded evidence package with provenance, retention, scope, and chain-of-custody metadata.
Trace each claim back to source evidence without direct production access.
Verify export completeness for a named framework, tenant, and time window.
forbidden_actions: browse live tenant data outside approved package
access unrelated tenants or internal-only operator runbooks
modify or extend evidence package retention

identity_and_authorization.authorization_rule: Server-side Cedar/PDP decisions must include tenant_id, role, purpose, evidence_class, data_class, and publishability_state. Client-side filtering is presentation-only and never the tenant boundary.

data_classes.redaction: No tenant names, raw logs, or private incident details unless explicitly public.
Collapse internal file paths, exploit payloads, secrets, and employee identities to evidence refs and roles.

data_classes.default_visibility: explicit export grant or auditor room only
data_classes.redaction: Apply pack-specific residency, consent, retention, and regulator disclosure policy before export.
Never directly customer-visible; publish derived summary only when approved by policy.

cross_tenant_rules: Queries must include tenant_id from trusted auth context; tenant_id supplied in request payload is an assertion to check, not authority.
Evidence aggregation across tenants is operator-only and cannot back a tenant-visible export without per-tenant decomposition.
Shared-service evidence must render as tenant-impact scope plus shared-control proof; it must not reveal other tenants, cell occupancy, or noisy-neighbor details.

public_vs_authenticated_boundary.public_status_surface: Public status links and summaries may be embedded in the portal but remain governed by ADR-0168.
public_vs_authenticated_boundary.authenticated_trust_surface: Compliance evidence, SBOM/VEX posture, control freshness, DPA artifacts, and audit exports require tenant-scoped authentication and authorization.
public_vs_authenticated_boundary.outage_mode: The public status page must remain reachable during auth outages; authenticated evidence room may degrade read-only or unavailable without changing public status authority.

customer_visible_summary: signed SBOM presence by releasable artifact
blocking vulnerability count by customer-safe class
exception expiry and remediation SLA class

evidence_source_map.trust_center_component: Status, SLO, DR, incident, and postmortem posture
customer_visible_summary: SLO/DR evidence state by service or pack

operator_only_detail: raw CI logs containing paths or usernames

api_contract.canonical_surface: cloud-native authenticated API plus customer/admin web UX; no legacy CLI authority

endpoint_groups.authorization: tenant_admin, security_compliance_reviewer with active grant, oyatie_operator scoped to tenant

endpoint_groups.purpose: Customer-safe evidence detail with source refs, audit-chain refs, redaction state, and non-claim boundary.
endpoint_groups.authorization: same as evidence_index plus evidence-specific data_class permit

endpoint_groups.purpose: SBOM and VEX posture by artifact/release without exposing raw scanner output or exploit detail.
endpoint_groups.authorization: tenant_admin or reviewer grant with security-evidence scope

endpoint_groups.purpose: Control freshness badges by evidence source, lane, compliance pack, service, and tenant/cell scope.
endpoint_groups.authorization: tenant_admin or reviewer grant with control-evidence scope

endpoint_groups.purpose: Activated pack view with regulator references, data classes, retention, residency, DR floors, and breach workflow pointers.
endpoint_groups.authorization: tenant_admin or reviewer grant with compliance scope

endpoint_groups.authorization: tenant_admin; operator approval required for regulated export scopes until policy says otherwise

endpoint_groups.authorization: tenant_admin and oyatie_operator scoped to tenant

query_and_pagination_rules: All list endpoints require server-side tenant scoping from trusted auth context.
Pagination cursors must be opaque and bound to tenant_id, actor, filters, and expiry.
Sorting by freshness, evidence_class, compliance_pack_id, service_id, and last_updated_trusted is required for the first UI slice.
Unknown source-system state renders as blocked_missing_evidence rather than hidden success.

information_architecture.label: Trust Center overview
information_architecture.empty_state_rule: Show missing/stale/not-yet-implemented evidence explicitly with claim_tier=target_non_claim or spec_ready; never render an empty green dashboard.

information_architecture.label: Controls and evidence
information_architecture.empty_state_rule: Controls without current evidence render blocked_missing_evidence or blocked_stale_evidence.

information_architecture.label: SBOM and vulnerability posture
information_architecture.empty_state_rule: Missing signed SBOM or missing VEX maps to blocked_missing_evidence, not pass.

information_architecture.label: Status, incidents, SLO, and DR
information_architecture.empty_state_rule: If status/SLO/DR evidence is target-only, label as target_non_claim and link the required evidence gap.

information_architecture.label: Exports and auditor room
components: two-person or operator approval state for regulated exports
information_architecture.empty_state_rule: Export unavailable must show policy reason and safe next step, not route around approval.

information_architecture.label: Operator publishability queue
information_architecture.empty_state_rule: No blocked items is an operator queue state only; tenant green posture still depends on source evidence.

accessibility_and_browser_expectations: Keyboard-navigable evidence table, filter chips, export wizard, modal/dialog flows, and status/error alerts.
WCAG 2.2 AA contrast for freshness and status badges; do not encode pass/fail solely by color.
Screen-reader labels for claim tier, freshness state, evidence source, and exception expiry.
Responsive layout for admin console widths and narrow reviewer-share links.
Browser/user-story verification must cover tenant admin invite, reviewer evidence read, SBOM/VEX view, export request, and access-audit review.
best_in_class_benchmarks: AWS Artifact for compliance reports and agreements
Google Cloud Compliance Reports Manager and Assured Workloads evidence framing
Microsoft Service Trust Portal / Purview Compliance Manager for control mapping and artifacts
Cloudflare Trust Hub for security/compliance posture and public assurances
Atlassian Statuspage/GitHub Status/Stripe Status for status and incident UX patterns

freshness_and_claim_status.externally_certified_rule: Allowed only when an approved external attestation/audit artifact exists, is tenant/policy applicable, and legal/compliance permits display. This spec creates no certified status.

default_freshness_targets.override_source: /specs/security-validation-pipeline-matrix.json lane cadence or compliance pack if stricter
/specs/vulnerability-intelligence-sbom-vex-pipeline.json required advisory feed freshness and remediation SLA
pack version, regulator update cadence, or source-row refresh cadence if stricter

default_freshness_targets.warning_after: PT15M for live status; P30D for DR drill posture unless pack stricter
default_freshness_targets.stale_after: PT1H for live status; overdue when drill cadence exceeded

badge_rules: Green/current badges require source evidence, trusted timestamp, claim tier, and audit_event_ref.
Spec-ready or target-only evidence uses neutral/info badges, never success badges.
Stale or missing blocking sources dominate aggregate summaries even when other categories are current.
Exception badges must display expiry and reviewer role; expired exceptions return the underlying item to blocked/stale state.

pack_fields_to_portal_sections.visibility: tenant-scoped; export package includes audit refs
tenant-scoped summary plus exportable policy evidence
summary only unless policy fragment is approved for export

pack_activation_rules: Tenant portal shows only packs activated, offered, or requested for that tenant and region.
Inactive packs may render as not_applicable or available-to-request; they must not imply control coverage.
Pack-specific floors override generic freshness, retention, export, and DR display defaults when stricter.
Jurisdiction-specific artifacts require residency-aware storage and export routing before display.

exception_rules: Every visible exception cites source exception/VEX record, approver role, expiry, compensating controls, and audit_event_ref.
Expired exceptions cannot remain green; UI and API recalculate freshness/publishability from the current source state.
Operator publishability decisions are append-only records with reviewer identity, reason, source refs, and expiry when temporary.
Trust Center exports include a manifest with source evidence refs and audit-chain refs, not mutable screenshots as sole proof.
retention_rules: Access-audit records retain at least 400 days unless compliance pack requires longer.
Regulated export evidence follows pack retention floors and legal hold policy.
Reviewer grants are revocable and expire by default; exports must carry expiry and revocation metadata when technically enforceable.

first_minimal_slice.goal: Deliver a tenant-scoped evidence index with SBOM/VEX posture and control freshness badges before broader auditor-room/export automation.
included_capabilities: tenant-scoped evidence index API and read model
public status link/embed and status freshness indicator
basic tenant admin UX with reviewer read-only grant
access audit for evidence views and grants
excluded_until_later_slices: operator publishability automation beyond manual review queue
minimum_acceptance: Cross-tenant negative tests fail closed for every API endpoint and UI route.
Missing/stale evidence renders as blocked or warning, never green/hidden.
SBOM/VEX view refuses to publish raw scanner output and shows signed SBOM/VEX state only.
Control freshness badges include source_system, trusted timestamp, evidence_ref, and audit_event_ref.
Keyboard and screen-reader user stories pass for evidence table, filters, detail pane, and reviewer grant flow.

security_privacy_review_criteria: Tenant isolation negative tests cover list, detail, export, reviewer grant, access audit, status embed, and stale cursor replay.
Evidence detail pages cannot reveal secrets, raw PII, exploit payloads, private incident notes, raw scanner output, or other tenant identifiers.
Authorization decisions are server-side and auditable; disabled client controls are not relied on for enforcement.
Export packages require purpose, time window, actor, expiry, approval state, manifest, and audit-chain references.
Claim-tier and non-certification boundaries are present in API and UI for every readiness/compliance/security posture summary.
Failure modes are fail-closed: missing source evidence, stale evidence, parser errors, unknown applicability, and expired exceptions do not render green.
verification_plan: JSON syntax validation for this spec and root-hub/registry updates.
Board search confirms no active trust-center card already covered this exact product/control-plane surface before TRUSTCENTER-001.
Follow-up implementation cards exist and are linked to TRUSTCENTER-001 with API, UI, ingestion, and docs/security review acceptance paths.

First implementation PRs must include API/contract replay, cross-tenant negative tests, browser/accessibility user-story evidence, and independent security/privacy review before any tenant-facing launch claim.
No generated JSON is hand-edited and no legacy oya CLI merge or trust-center authority is introduced.
